keyPoints: Every step has a key point
Give each step at least one key point
safety: Hazards have a safety key point
Add a Safety key point where the step names a hazard
takt: Give the takt and a time for every step, and keep the total within it
steps: Keep it to 12 steps or fewer: split the job in two
reasons: Every key point has a reason
Write the reason for each key point
changeNote: The version has a change note
Write what changed in this version

tips: A major step is what is done, in a few words. If it needs a sentence, it is two steps.
Key points make or break the job.
Only what affects safety, quality, technique or cost. Everything else is training detail.
Every key point has a reason.
People keep a rule they understand. Write why, in the words of the floor.
Change the standard, not the people.
When the job changes, start a new version with a note, then train the team on it.

doc.title: Close the day in the night audit
doc.ppe: Property management system, cash drawer, report folder

steps.step: Close the restaurant and bar cheques

points.text: Every open cheque posted to a room or paid
points.reason: An open cheque is lost revenue once the day is closed

points.text: Each reservation not arrived is checked against its guarantee
points.reason: A guaranteed no-show is charged, a non-guaranteed one is cancelled

points.text: Charge the no-show fee by the policy, with the card authorised
points.reason: A missed no-show fee is money that never comes back

points.text: Count with the back-office door closed and the safe locked
points.reason: Cash counted in view of the lobby invites a robbery

points.text: Cash matches the system to the cent; any difference is written down
points.reason: A difference found tomorrow can no longer be explained

points.text: Start the close only when every terminal is logged out
points.reason: A terminal still logged in blocks or splits the close

points.text: Manager report, cash report and in-house list in the folder
points.reason: The morning shift and the manager read the day from these reports

steps.step: Hand over to the morning shift

points.text: Open issues written in the handover book with room numbers
points.reason: What is only said is forgotten by noon

doc.title: Take over a delivery at the dock
doc.ppe: Safety shoes, high-visibility vest, gloves; pallet truck, scanner, camera

points.text: Wheels chocked and engine off before anyone opens the doors
points.reason: A truck that moves while the doors open crushes the person behind it

points.text: Seal number matches the delivery note
points.reason: A broken or wrong seal means the load may have been opened

points.text: Walking speed, nobody else in the trailer while unloading
points.reason: A pallet that slips has nowhere to go but onto feet

points.text: Unload from the back, pallet straight on the forks
points.reason: A twisted pallet catches the trailer wall

steps.step: Count the pallets and check for damage

points.text: Count against the delivery note, a photo of every damage
points.reason: Damage not recorded at the dock becomes the warehouse's cost

points.text: Damage written on the delivery note before signing
points.reason: The carrier pays only for damage written on the note

steps.step: Sign and give the driver the copy

points.text: Remarks written above the signature
points.reason: A clean signature accepts the load as perfect

points.text: Chocks removed only once the doors are closed and the dock is clear
points.reason: The driver cannot see the dock from the cab

example.title: Load a roll cage onto the truck
example.ppe: Safety shoes, gloves, high-visibility vest; scanner, load bar
example.changeNote: Step 2: walkway away from the forklift lane added after a near miss at dock 3.

history.note: Step 6: scan the cage label, not a parcel on it.

points.text: Wheels turn freely and both brakes hold
points.reason: A cage with a broken brake rolls back off the tail lift

points.text: Cage label matches the load list
points.reason: A wrong label sends the cage to the wrong store

steps.step: Push the cage to the dock door

points.text: Push, never pull, both hands on the frame
points.reason: Pulling puts your feet in front of the wheels

points.text: Stay on the marked walkway, out of the forklift lane
points.reason: A forklift driver cannot see a person behind a cage

steps.step: Check the dock leveller and the truck

points.text: Truck wheels chocked, dock light green, leveller resting on the truck floor
points.reason: A truck that moves off drops the cage and the person into the gap

steps.step: Roll the cage onto the truck

points.text: One cage at a time, steered from the back corner
points.reason: Two cages at once can neither be steered nor stopped

points.text: Heaviest cages against the front wall
points.reason: Weight at the front keeps the load stable when the driver brakes

points.text: Tight against the cage before, no gap
points.reason: A gap lets the cages move and tip over in transit

points.text: Brakes on, load bar fitted at chest height
points.reason: A loose cage falls on whoever opens the doors at the store

points.text: Scan the cage label, not a parcel on it
points.reason: The store sees which cage is on which truck only from the cage label

steps.step: Close the load and hand over

points.text: Cage count matches the load list before the doors close
points.reason: A missing cage is found here, not at the store

points.text: Empty cages from the truck back to the return line
points.reason: Every lost roll cage costs about 150 euros
